answer.generated: The cache coherence problem in multiprocessor systems arises due to the independent caching of shared data by each processor. As processors cache shared data independently, they may hold different versions of the same memory location, leading to inconsistencies when multiple processors attempt to read or write to the same data simultaneously. This issue is exacerbated because each processor operates based on its local cache, resulting in potential conflicts and requiring mechanisms to ensure all processors have a consistent view of the shared data.
